Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided following the prepared remarks. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Karen Walsh, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Information Officer; David Lee, Chief Human Resources Officer; and Monica Ruiz, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on eight key aspects: operating margin guidance for the next quarter and year, the impact of cost reduction initiatives, capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, total admissions and patient days year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, the impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, the impact of seasonality or external factors such as flu season, and net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.

Let me start with our operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year. We delivered a strong Q3 operating margin of 12.8%, up 110 basis points year-over-year, thanks to robust procedural volumes and disciplined cost management even as labor inflation moderated. This is our sixth straight quarter of margin expansion, placing us at the high end among hospital peers like HCA and Tenet. For Q1 2025, we expect margins between 13.0% and 14.0%, a sequential step-up supported by 3-5% quarter-over-quarter patient volume growth from pent-up demand in high-acuity electives like orthopedics, cardiology interventions, and oncology infusions, which boast margins over 25%. Same-facility admissions should rise 2-3%, with adjusted admissions up 4-5%, in line with CMS's 2.9% IPPS update for FY2025. On costs, non-labor expenses will grow under 3% via our Vizient supply chain partnership, with multi-year contracts on orthopedic implants and pharmaceuticals saving $45 million annually, akin to Community Health Systems' Vizient gains. Labor, at 55% of revenue, should improve as wage inflation eases to 3.5% from 5.2%, powered by our ShiftMed AI workforce platform and Epic MyChart predictive analytics that cut agency RN use by 25% in Q3. Our Sunbelt markets—Florida and Texas, 60% of our 45-hospital network—drive this with 15-16% Q1 margins from 55% commercial mix versus the national 48%, plus strong Medicare Advantage from UnitedHealth and Humana. Northeast and Midwest sites expect 10-11% amid Medicaid redeterminations and New York rate issues, offset by outpatient joint bundles. For full-year 2025, we're guiding 13.5% to 14.5% margins, up 70-100 basis points from 2024's 12.9%, on $8.2-8.4 billion revenue and 18-19% EBITDA. Levers include revenue cycle RPA with Waystar cutting collections to 45 days from 52 for $30 million AR recovery like Tenet; ASC growth with five de novos and two tuck-ins targeting 20%+ margins amid 15% elective rebound per Definitive Healthcare; and 4-5% commercial rate hikes despite Medicare sequestration and No Surprises Act disputes. We're baking in 6% pharma inflation on 340B drugs and OPPS cuts, but $200 million buybacks and 3.0x leverage provide flexibility. This positions us ahead of Universal Health Services' flatter guidance due to their labor exposure.

Next, the impact of our cost reduction initiatives has been transformative, delivering $185 million in year-over-year sequential savings that expanded adjusted EBITDA margins 220 basis points to 18.7%, our best in three years. This countered inflation and funded growth in ASCs and value-based care. Labor, 55% of expenses, saw $112 million saved—a 12% agency drop—by cutting contract labor to 3.1% from 8.2%, a 62% plunge amid post-COVID RN wage hikes of 15-20% per NSI data. Our Clinical Ladder upskilled 4,200 staff via Chamberlain University ties, dropping turnover to 16% from 22% with 3.5x ROI on $15 million. Epic forecasting and ML models hit 92% fill rates from 78%, slashing ICU overtime 28%, especially in Sunbelt flu surges. Southeast saved $65 million with low unions; Northeast $22 million via bonuses linked to HACRP. Labor fell to 52.3% of revenue, down 310 basis points. Supplies saved $48 million, 9% below inflation despite GLP-1 shortages and implant volatility per GHX. Premier GPO standardized 78% top SKUs for 11% concessions like HCA; Vizient VMI and RFID cut stockouts 41% and $28 million inventory, with 22% ortho waste reduction. Sunbelt saved $28 million near J&J hubs; Midwest $12 million via auctions. SG&A dropped 7% to $420 million or 11.2% of revenue, with $25 million from Change Healthcare AI denials cutting AR days to 42 from 48 and denials to 8.5%, capturing $18 million from UnitedHealthcare DRG rebills up 15%; Cerner optimizations saved $9 million IT; divesting two rural hospitals like Tenet yielded $7 million. Offsets included $75 million wage pressure, 5% pharma, 1.2% MA compression at 1.68 CMI. West Coast saved less at 8% due to AB 3129, but VBC shared $42 million. We expect $200 million more savings in 2024, 60% recurring, reinvesting 40% in 15 ASCs for 35% margins versus 15% inpatient, dropping leverage to 3.2x from 3.8x amid No Surprises shifts.

Capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion totaled $285 million this quarter, up 18% year-over-year and 22% of adjusted EBITDA, reflecting high-ROI discipline amid demographics, tech, and reimbursements. Modernization was 62% or $177 million, up 25% for efficiency and outcomes in our 45 hospitals. $65 million for Siemens 3T MRIs and dual-source CTs in 12 Southeast sites boosted throughput 30% and AI diagnostics via GE Edison for oncology/cardio, 45% of revenue. $42 million for seven da Vinci Xi robots in Atlanta/Dallas cut LOS 22%, lifted CMI 15% for MS-DRG gains. $28 million Epic/Nuance AI scribing in 80% beds saves 12% labor. Sunbelt capex $4.2 million/bed at 55% revenue, 2.5% pop growth, 42% MA; Midwest $22 million HVAC for sepsis ROI under 24 months. Expansion $108 million: $45 million three Texas/NC ASCs adding 18 ORs to 85% utilization Year 2, 25-30% margins vs. 15% inpatient for 20% outpatient CAGR. $32 million Phoenix 120-bed tower for neuro-ICU/behavioral amid 18% uninsured; $18 million LEED pavilions with solar for IRA credits. Blended IRR 14-16%, payback 3.8 years vs. peer 4.5 per Becker's, prioritizing cardio/ortho/oncology. Full-year guide $1.15-1.2 billion, 55-60% modernization for 400-450 bps EBITDA expansion like Tenet's Vanguard.

On same-facility admissions and patient day growth, excluding M&A like Texas/Florida tuck-ins, admissions rose 3.4% YoY and 1.9% QoQ across 185 hospitals/1,200 outpatients in 28 states—eighth straight YoY positive, best QoQ since Q4 2022. Patient days up 3.1% YoY/1.6% QoQ, CMI to 1.82 from 1.79 on cardio/ortho; adjusted days 4.2% YoY outpacing AHA's 1.8%. QoQ lapped weak Q2 allergies/priors; LOS 4.7 days flat. Southeast 5.1% YoY admissions/4.7% days on 58% commercial, post-hurricane electives, Medtronic spine. Midwest 1.2%/0.9% on flu/RSV to ERs, oncology via Sarah Cannon. Southwest 4.8% on MA stability at 32%. Digital front-door ApexOne/MyChart up pre-adms 22%, 3x ROI on $45 million. ACO REACH 1.2M lives cut readmits to 14.8%, +60 bps days. LeanTaaS iQueue cut no-shows 18%, +1,100 days; turnover 12% from 18%. Priors delayed ortho 2.8%; 340B 4.5% risk. Q4 guide 3.5-4.0% admissions/3.0-3.5% days on flu normalize, $250M outpatient capex for 10% CMI bundles.

Total admissions hit 128,450, up 4.8% YoY from 122,600 and 2.3% QoQ from 125,500; EPDs 782,300, +5.1% YoY/+2.7% QoQ, ALOS 6.09 flat, adjusted amns 6.2% YoY. Surgical 7.2% YoY to 42,100/3.1% QoQ on Stryker Mako 12% throughput/CMI 1.82; medical 3.9%/1.8% to 71,900 respiratory/cardio; behavioral 5.5% to 14,450. Southeast 8.1%/8.6% snowbirds/Tampa hybrid; Southwest 4.2%/1.2% hurricane; Midwest/Northeast 2.1% Medicaid/flu, tele reduced 15%. Organic 3.8%+1.0% M&A; 48% commercial +150bps, 32% MA; Qventus cut variability 18%/4% CMI. Capacity/staffing headwinds. Q4 3.5-5.0% amns/4.0-5.5% EPDs, $300M capex 500 ICU/Teladoc for share.

Value-based care contracts drove 28% of net revenue, up from 22% YoY/$1.2B quarterly across acute/outpatient/post-acute. MA 65% Medicare VBC at 32M lives/50% eligibles. MSSP Track 3 120k lives $145M 2023 savings/75% share, 2.1% premium, Q2 $38M on 14.2% readmits vs. 15.9%. Commercial 18%, Optum 250k/Humana CJR 104-108% on 4.2-star/92% protocols, 1.8% lift. Southeast 35%/$22M SNF cuts; Midwest 12% tele pilots 1.5% HEDIS. CoreValue Palantir/Cerner NLP 22% HCC/$75M RAF; AI readmits -18%. +60bps EBITDA, $12M downside. To 35%/$500M by 2026, 90% derisked, ahead HCA 24%/Tenet 20%.

Seasonality and external factors like flu boosted respiratory admissions 17.8% YoY/12% total or 14,200 cases/$285M revenue at $20,100/case—strongest since FY2021. Admissions +11.2% to 142k, ED +19.4% to 2.1M like HCA/Tenet; respiratory ALOS 4.2, CMI 1.78 +2.3%; obs +22%/28% ratio. Midwest 25% flu belt H3N2; Sunbelt 9% vax 52%; Northeast RSV peds. +220bps EBITDA to 14.8%, revenue +13.4% to $4.2B Medicare $14,200/commercial $28,500; antivirals +15%/$22M, labor +9%/180bps, 52% gov mix. RSV +32%, weather hypothermia. Epic/Google Vertex 92% predict, FluFlex +16% RN; Vizient 150k doses. FluGuard/CVS 1.2M shots -22% absenteeism/HEDIS. $450M 1,200 beds 30% resp ICUs. Q1 -5-7%, tele-ED 15%.

Finally, net patient revenue was $2.52 billion, +8.2% YoY from $2.33B/+5.7% QoQ from $2.38B on acute recovery/RCM. Volumes +4.1%, amns +3.8% to 48,200 ortho/cardio 28%; CMI +2.2% to 1.85 MS-DRG 470/981; OPV +5.3% to 1.2M/12% ASCs. Rev/adm +4.0% to $28,450/OPV +2.9% to $1,210; managed +3.5% vs. IPPS 2.7%; Medicare 98%/Medicaid 92%; commercial 38% BCBS/UHC. Deductions 28.4% from 30.1%, bad debt -15% to $85M/1.7%, collections 42% Waystar/MyChart 96% priors. QoQ seasonal resp +4.2% ADC 2,450, surgical +7%, tele 22% OPV <5% no-shows. Southeast +11% to $1.1B 45% comm/Humana; Midwest +4% $650M Medicaid; West +9% 25% MA. Epic RCM AR 42/denials -22%; 15 VBC 2M lives 4-star; $150M robotics CMI. Q4 7-9% YoY, $500M M&A.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Reynolds. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Reynolds mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.52 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $2.20 billion, representing 87.3% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $215 million, or $1.72 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our bundled payment program has shown remarkable results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-driven scheduling and supply chain standardization, which have resulted in significant cost savings, improved patient flow, and enhanced staff productivity.

Next, Karen Walsh will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Karen Walsh:
Thank you, Tom. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets, enhance our service offerings, and diversify our revenue streams.

After that, Raj Singh will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Karen. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and mitigate the risk of data breaches. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions to improve scalability and flexibility.

Following that, David Lee will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

David Lee:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives to improve employee satisfaction, enhance training and development opportunities, and promote a culture of diversity and inclusion.

Finally, Monica Ruiz will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

Monica Ruiz:
Thank you, David. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy, and prevent fraud and abuse.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions: Press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

David Lee:
Thanks for the question, John. We're prioritizing a multi-faceted approach, including expanding our Clinical Ladder program that upskills thousands of staff with university partners, reducing turnover significantly. We've also rolled out AI predictive staffing for better work-life balance, regional retention bonuses tied to quality metrics, and diversity training. Employee surveys show satisfaction up 15%, with engagement scores in the top quartile for the industry.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

Monica Ruiz:
Great question, Maria. Our comprehensive program includes regular audits, AI-driven risk monitoring integrated with Epic, and staff-wide training on HIPAA and No Surprises Act. For cyber, we've layered multi-factor auth, endpoint detection from partners like CrowdStrike, and annual penetration tests. We've had zero major breaches, and we're ahead on CMS interoperability rules, with incident response times under 4 hours.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Karen Walsh:
Absolutely, David. Our tuck-ins like the recent Texas and Florida hospitals add high-acuity volumes immediately, boosting same-facility growth while we integrate ASCs for 20%+ margins. These enhance our Sunbelt footprint, diversify payers with more MA, and yield 3-4x synergies in supply chain and RCM. Long-term, they support 5-7% revenue CAGR, de-risking against inpatient shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Emily Patel:
Thanks, Alex. Our GE Edison and Nuance pilots with Siemens imaging analyze scans for oncology and cardio, reducing false negatives by 18% and speeding workflows. Integrated with Epic, it flags high-risk cases pre-admission, lifting CMI and outcomes. Early results show 12% better early detection rates, aligning with VBC quality gates.

Operator:
Thank you. As a final question from Chris Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel:
Given the strong volume guidance, how do you see capex evolving into 2025?

Lisa Chen:
Good question, Chris. We're guiding $1.15-1.2 billion full-year, with modernization like robotics and AI at 55-60%. Into 2025, we'll hold flat as a percentage of EBITDA, focusing expansions on ASCs and ICUs for 14-16% IRR. This funds margin expansion without leverage creep.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
